code.enroll.deny_text: The explorer also redacts files matching these globs (a name like *.secret, or a path tail like config/prod.yml), on top of the built-in secret list.
code.enroll.drop_text: Stop redacting .env files and private keys in the explorer, keeping only your own globs; it prevents accidents and is not a boundary against the agent.
code.enroll.fixed_note: These are fixed when the machine enrolls. Loosening one later means enrolling again; {#code}galopin policy set{/code} on the machine can only tighten.
code.enroll.free_text: List and accept models from providers other than the gateway's, so spend can land outside the account this machine enrolled under.
code.enroll.install_opencode_text: The agent runs the opencode binary as its coding engine — check this on a fresh machine that does not have it yet (leave it unchecked if it is already installed).
code.enroll.max_terminals_problem: {problem} Until fixed, the printed command leaves the default of 8.
code.enroll.no_files_text: Keep the /code explorer out of this machine's workspace files.
code.enroll.no_tools_text: Install none of galopin's agent tools (session_list, session_read, session_spawn, session_send and the schedule tools), so sessions cannot find, read, start or message each other, or manage your schedules.
code.enroll.outside_label: Agents may work outside the project folder without asking.
code.enroll.outside_text: By default an agent asks before reading or writing files outside the workspace folder; ticked, it doesn't.
code.enroll.provider_text: Leave opencode's built-in providers enabled beside the gateway's models.
code.enroll.roots_text: Only these folders, and anything below them, can be opened as a workspace; with none listed, anywhere can.
code.enroll.secrets_label: Agents may read secret files without asking.
code.enroll.secrets_text: By default an agent asks before reading .env and similar files; ticked, it reads them like any other file, so their contents reach the model.
code.enroll.shell_text: On by default. A slash command whose template runs a shell snippet (!`git diff`, say) may run it, inside opencode and before any permission is asked: the snippet is code from the repo. Plain slash commands work either way.
code.enroll.subagents_text: On by default. A task can keep running after its parent turn ends, with its result handed back later.
code.enroll.terminals_off: Terminal is off for this deployment: none is offered until an administrator turns it on ({#code}./configure --terminal{/code}). This box decides what this machine allows then.
code.enroll.terminals_text: On by default. The panel can open a real shell on this machine: anyone who controls your Cerea session can run commands as you, with no model and no permission rule in the way.
code.enroll.title: What this machine will ever allow
code.enroll.trust_label: Trust the repos this machine opens.
code.enroll.trust_text: A repo you cloned can carry its own assistant setup — extra commands, helpers and connections — which normally stays switched off, because those are someone else's files. Turn this on only where you trust the repos. Your AI provider stays locked to our gateway either way.

workspace.local.howto.approve_note: It appears under {#em}Waiting for approval{/em} as soon as it checks in. After you approve it, its servers show in the MCP panel and the composer, labelled with the machine's name. {#link}More about local connectors{/link}.
workspace.local.howto.bullet_allowed: {#code}allowedTools{/code} is the machine's ceiling: only those tools are offered and any other call is refused on the machine, whatever the chat asks. Leave it out to offer every tool.
workspace.local.howto.bullet_command: {#code}command{/code} starts a {#strong}stdio{/strong} server; {#code}"type": "http"{/code} with a {#code}url{/code} reaches an {#strong}http{/strong} one (headers and {#code}{var}{/code} from the machine's environment work as in Claude Code).
workspace.local.howto.bullet_description: {#code}description{/code} and {#code}disabled: true{/code} are shown here and in the MCP panel; Claude ignores them.
workspace.local.howto.bullet_edits: Edits are picked up without a restart. A server that asks for OAuth is signed in from the MCP panel; its tokens stay on the machine.
workspace.local.howto.config_note: The file is in galopin's config directory, next to {#code}credentials.json{/code}: {#code}~/.config/galopin/mcp.json{/code} on Linux, {#code}~/Library/Application Support/galopin/mcp.json{/code} on macOS. It is the format Claude Desktop and Claude Code use, so an existing file can be copied as is, or point galopin at another file: {#code}galopin run --mcp-config /path/to/claude_desktop_config.json{/code}
workspace.local.howto.enroll_note: Opens your browser to sign in with this deployment's identity provider (or prints a link and code for another device). A connectors machine needs no coding agent, no opencode and no billing group.
workspace.local.howto.install_note: The installer comes from this deployment and puts {#code}galopin{/code} in {#code}~/.local/bin{/code}.
workspace.local.howto.intro: Run an MCP server on your own machine (a notes folder, a database, a tool on a private network) and use it from your chats. Nothing is opened to the internet: the machine dials out to {name}.
workspace.local.howto.service: Keep it running as a service (Linux)
workspace.local.howto.service_note: A service does not read your shell profile: put the directories your servers' commands need in {#code}PATH{/code} and any {#code}{var}{/code} an entry uses in the unit's {#code}Environment={/code}. On macOS use the launchd file {#code}org.cerea.galopin.plist{/code} from the Cerea repository's {#code}agent/packaging/{/code}.
workspace.local.howto.service_save: Stop the copy you started by hand, save this as {#code}~/.config/systemd/user/galopin.service{/code}, then start it:
workspace.local.howto.signin_note: Open this chat and sign in with the same account. Cerea only accepts a machine for an account it has seen, so {#code}galopin run{/code} is refused (403) until you have.
workspace.local.howto.step2: Enroll it as a connectors machine
workspace.local.howto.step3: Sign in to Cerea in your browser once before running galopin
workspace.local.howto.step5: List the servers it offers in mcp.json
workspace.local.howto.title: Connect a machine
workspace.local.login_help: If the provider refuses this page's redirect, run {#code}galopin connectors login {name}{/code} on the machine.
